title: The Last Night
description: The last night in Lagos before the festival: a farewell the Chief didn't send, a message from Ike, and two phone calls that matter.

beats.speaker: chiefOdu
beats.text: (at your door, which he has never visited before) Going home, brother? For the yams? (He smiles.) Abundance loves festivals. So many people in one place. We will see you there.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A white car is parked opposite your door all evening. Nobody gets out. Nobody needs to.

beats.speaker: usher
beats.text: (from the car window, as you pass) We remember the bridge. Enjoy your festival, Emeka.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (a voice note, wind behind it, a sea somewhere) Emeka. I'm in Ghana. I fry plantain at a beach bar. Yesterday a customer slipped on a peel and I... I nearly laughed. Nearly. (A long breath.) Go home. Don't let them have yours.

beats.speaker: mamaIke
beats.text: (on the phone, from Nkwọ-Agụụ) Emeka, my son, have you seen Ike? He sends money every month and never calls. This month the money came. No call. A mother can count both.

options.text: Tell her the truth about the white cars.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: You're coming for the festival. (A long pause on the line.) I need to tell you something before you arrive, so you don't hear it from my father first.

variants.text: (She is right there, folding your shirts into the bag better than you did.) Nkwọ-Agụụ. Together. Like we said.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: You asked me for one year. It's been eight months. I'm still counting. I'm good at counting. (She doesn't say what the counting will decide.)

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: You asked me to come to Lagos, that week, at the burial. I didn't come. I wanted to see if you would ask again. You didn't.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: You told me kind is rare. I thought about it every day. You were right. (Her voice breaks a little.) You were also wrong.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: (a voice note, very tired) Come home, my son. Come home and let me look at you. Whatever you have done in Lagos, bring it. I am your mother. I have room.

variants.text: (a voice note, very tired) You told me the real Lagos at the burial. I have been praying about the man in white every night since. Come home. Bring all of it. The village knows things Lagos forgot.
(a voice note, very tired) You said Lagos was good to you. Your voice said something else. Come home, my son. Mothers don't need the words.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You remember the dibia: "Come back at the festival. Not before." It is the festival. It is time.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At 5 a.m. Bíọ́dún hoots outside. God's Time Is The Best, washed, decorated with ribbons for the Onitsha wedding. He has packed you a bag of agege bread "for the road and for your mother".

beats.title: The Last Night
beats.summary: Every voice you love, and every voice you fear, said the same thing tonight: come home. The road is open. So is the fire.
